content: I have been working a chat server called roc-chat. It's based largely on a zig-based server that I have been running since April. I technically deployed it today, but it's still a little rough around the edges. I will invite folks in the next couple days.
For now here is a taste of the code: https://github.com/showell/roc-chat/blob/main/app/GitHubSignUp.roc
Both the original zig server and the new Roc server were written by Claude. I worked on Zulip for over a decade, so the server draws on Zulip influences to a minor degree. It has topics.

Unlike Zulip, which does HTTP long-polling for live updates, the roc-chat program uses SSE (server sent events). It's live-update system is home grown but mildly inspired by things like datastar and htmx. It's pretty ordinary JS on the client side operating on mostly HTML payloads.

Unlike Zulip, which has a zillion dependencies, my server is very slim:

  • Zig: there's no build.zig.zon, so no Zig packages. The build links no system libraries, not even libc, and the deploy builds a static musl binary with Zig alone. Password hashing, HMAC, SHA-256, TLS for GitHub and the HTTP server all come from Zig's standard library.
  • Roc: the only package is roc-markdown (mine haha, see #show and tell > two roc-markdowns ), plus roc-chat's own platform.
  • JavaScript: the scripts in app/*.js import nothing and load nothing from another site. The page's security policy allows scripts from roc-chat's own origin only.

Caveats, outside the code:

  • Zig version: the box builds with my patched Zig (0.17.0+patched.2). I haven't checked whether roc-chat needs any of those patches or would build on a stock 0.17.
  • Running it: production also leans on Caddy (the proxy and TLS), systemd, ssh/scp for the deploy, and GitHub for OAuth. GitHub is optional: without the client files, there's no GitHub sign-in.
  • Developing it: the gate and tools need Shale (my scripting language) and git. tools/glue.shale also needs a checkout of Roc's source at the pinned commit.

Anton said:

What an awesome real world Roc app Steve! It must be one of the biggest Roc projects out there.

It's the biggest Roc app I've written by 2x. The server piece in Roc is not the real challenge of writing a chat system, although it is important, so adversarial reviews would be helpful. A lot of the challenge for chat is product design (and I have my own taste on chat formed from a decade of using Zulip). All the visible pieces are more about JS choices than Roc choices. Roc would be more fun at scale, but chat communities don't challenge you on scale unless you make up problems that don't actually have to exist (cough Zulip cough).

For more details on the overall architecture see my Roc showcase page. Chat's at the top.

You may pentest it.

  • Scope: chat.lynrummy.com only, not lynrummy.com or roc.lynrummy.com, which share the same front server.
  • No denial of service or load testing, and keep request rates modest. It's one small box.
  • Only your own accounts: test with accounts you create, and don't read or change other people's messages, even if he finds a way.
  • Report privately, in a DM to me, before mentioning anything publicly, and give me time to fix it.

Regarding styling, apart from the login page, which has gotten no love, I prefer to style things myself with a pretty vanilla aesthetic. There's light mode and dark mode. I use almost no external CSS, because I hate how CSS bitrots and drifts. Instead, most of the styling is done thru small JS helpers directly on the DOM elements as they are created. Some things like hover effects are done with more CSS-like approaches.

I want to thank notramo for a thorough audit he did for roc-chat today. It found a couple serious bugs and many other flaws to address. All known issues are addressed on the production site. Fortunately, the site is mostly public or innocuous chat with very few users so far, but the audit led us to make important performance-related changes that will help at bigger scale.

I had Claude do a writeup of the measures taken today to improve how my Roc code handles things: https://roc.lynrummy.com/security-idioms/

I think it will be of interest to anybody writing secure apps where Roc does any heavy lifting (roc-chat definitely fits the bill). Richard Feldman Claude makes the case that linear types would help roc-chat for some pretty key things. It's toward the top, under "What we'd ask of Roc".

Folks from yesterday's meeting may appreciate how we use "proofs" through various gates to ensure security. There's nothing as formal as Lean or anything, but the combo of Roc and Shale seems sufficient to me. As always, I would love code review on the key pieces of code here. The article embeds Roc snippets with GH links.

linear types sound like something for #ideas - I am skeptical that it turns out to be a good idea, but I'm open to listening to what the explanation is for the motivating use cases where they would apparently help. :smile:

My ultimate goal for roc-chat is to get community involvement in building a better chat tool for us than Zulip. Zulip's fine. It's particularly well-tuned for this-sized community, and I haven't heard a single complaint about Zulip since I joined here.

But we can do better. Zulip is a big monolithic app built on top of Django that still doesn't support Roc syntax coloring, because they move slow. Folks should try out roc-chat.
Shouldn't we eat our own dog food for the one type of app that we all tautologically agree is useful?
https://blog.zulip.com/2026/11/19/zulip-server-13-3-security-release/

I'm keen to hear your thought on what a roadmap or plan might look like to get from here to a mature enough state for the Roc community, if we are thinking longer term about replacing Zulip. In the meantime I'm sure there are a lot of really cool projects we can collaborate on.

If you would consider roc-signals for the front-end, I think that might be a good fit. Joy also would work well too.

If I put my brainstorming cap on, I can think of crazy ideas like embedding REPL's into chat, or linking/integrating with things like Roclet or Rocco. Or crazier things like shaders for cool graphics.

If you have Roc on the front end you could render PDF's in the browser, or leverage the package ecosystem.

I've been doing all kinds of things, and I'm finding we usually have what I need already there (or 95% of the way there, and a small patch upstream is all we need).

Passkey support and end-to-end encryption for DMs would be nice to have.

Yeah, I see the need for that in certain DM conversations, but that would probably never be in the scope of roc-chat. It's a single-hosted platform (like Zulip). It's intended mostly for discussion. If you have folks that you want end-to-end encrypted DM conversations with, I think it's better to have something more peer-to-peer in nature. There are certainly pieces of roc-chat that you could steal to make the client experience more ergonomic, but that's all JS code, not Roc.
